key_insight: TRCGL-Net tackles long-tailed chest X-ray multi-label classification by combining synthetic tail-class data generation, lesion-focused feature/attention learning, and label co-occurrence modeling.
clinical_relevance: The approach may improve detection support for rare chest X-ray findings that are often under-recognized in imbalanced training data.
method: Text-guided conditional diffusion generates realistic tail-class X-ray images from disease semantics.
Channel reweighting and class-aware attention emphasize disease-relevant features and regions.
A graph convolution model captures label co-occurrence to propagate information across diagnoses.
evidence_signal: On the PadChest dataset, the method reported tail-class mAP of 0.4904, overall mAP of 0.4408, and mAUC of 0.8989, outperforming prior methods in the abstract.
watch_item: Synthetic data and label-dependency modeling may not generalize equally well across hospitals or imaging protocols without external validation.
paper_title: TRCGL-Net: A Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification Framework with Generative Data Augmentation and Label Co-Occurrence Modeling
